thread:
jason: quick question — for the internal inference API, are we leaning proto/gRPC-first or REST-first? browser clients + console UX make this fuzzy.
michelle: +1 to asking. main constraints: streaming latency, browser compatibility (gRPC-web/no-websockets customers), and consistent telemetry for rollouts.
ali: proto-first gives structured contracts and smaller payloads, but gRPC-web + Envoy adds friction for some integrations. fallback to JSON is required for a lot of our customers.
nora: telemetry point — if we have gateway-transcoding, where do quotas and per-route metrics live? gateway or runtime? we need token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
jason: open question: do we implement a gateway that translates REST<->gRPC (Envoy transcoder) or build lightweight adapters in the edge services?
michelle: gateway-transcoding is tempting. pros: single source of truth, can enforce quotas early. cons: opaque telemetry mapping, extra latencies, tricky streaming (SSE / chunked responses) mapping to gRPC streams.
ali: +1. also browser SDKs expect fetch/json or SSE for streaming. gRPC-web can't do true bidi streams in many browsers. We should standardize on server-sent-chunks for the browser path.
michelle: suggestion: two first-class surfaces — internal gRPC for services + managed REST/SSE for public/browser. Gateway does lightweight translation for unary calls and proxies streaming as chunked HTTP with a clear demarcation header.
jason: that sounds workable. what's the header shape we should use to keep tracing/quotas neat? example: X-RW-Client, X-RW-Tenant, X-RW-Route, X-RW-TraceId
nora: and persist original_content_type so console can show actual model output shape. e.g., X-RW-Orig-Content: application/protobuf
ali: example config snippet for routing policy we discussed:
```
route: inference
  match: /v1/generate
  prefer: grpc_internal: inference-service/v1.Generate
  fallback: http_json: /v1/generate
  quota: tenant.rate_per_min = 1200
  telemetry_keys: [route, tenant, model_version]
```
michelle: small nit — keep the fallback explicit so canary rollouts don't accidentally send traffic to the wrong model. console needs to display which surface served the request (grpc vs rest) and latency breakdown.
jason: telemetry naming: use rw.inference.tokens.{model}.{outcome} and rw.latency.{route}.{component} so we can slice in dashboards.
ali: question about schema evolution: if we go proto-first, do we generate JSON schemas for the REST surface? that will help validate client payloads and make console error messages actionable.
nora: yes — auto-generate JSON schema from protos. store schemas in catalog so console validations and example payloads work.
michelle: rollout UX: console should show canary live traffic % and let us toggle gateway translation on/off per-route, with a button to failover to REST directly. also surface per-route error types (transcoding_fail, model_error, timeout).
jason: implementation plan draft: 1) define proto contract for core inference RPCs, 2) implement internal gRPC runtime + telemetry hooks, 3) add Envoy-based gateway for REST<->gRPC with chunked streaming mapping, 4) auto-generate JSON schemas and wire console signals & quota enforcement, 5) canary toggle in console.
ali: risks: transcoding edge-cases (repeated fields, nested Any, streaming states). we'll need an examples test-suite.
ora: I'll add telemetry and quota requirements to the RFC doc and include sample metrics.
michelle: thanks — can someone create a spike to test chunked HTTP <-> grpc streaming with envoy? @ali interested? :eyes:
ali: I'll take the spike. will post initial results in this thread by EOD tomorrow.
dev-bot: deploy-checklist created: /boards/infra/spikes/1754123456-proxy-spike (automated) :robot_face:
jason: awesome. please include a tiny demo showing console view with route breakdown and which surface served each request.
michelle: thumbs up. end of thread for now — let's keep replies in-thread. :thumbsup:
